claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be homogenized into a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in initially BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by an interplay between thermodynamic driving forces for chemical ordering and diffusion kinetics.
Al is particularly involved in the proposed chemical ordering.
Cooling rate modulates the extent of atomic rearrangement in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Rapid cooling limits atomic diffusion and suppresses chemical ordering.
Rapid cooling preserves the high-temperature BCC phase as a metastable retained phase.
Slow cooling or intermediate-temperature holding increases atomic mobility and permits more chemical ordering.
The extent of Al-associated chemical ordering modulates the nucleation barrier for phase transformation.
Sufficient diffusion during slow cooling enables the nucleation barrier to be overcome.
Slow cooling drives transformation from high-temperature BCC to more thermodynamically stable phases.
The products enabled by slow cooling may include ordered B2 or other secondary phases.
Rapidly cooled samples are predicted to remain predominantly BCC.
Slowly cooled samples are predicted to show ordered or secondary phases in diffraction and microstructural measurements.
Rapidly quenched samples provide a baseline with minimal atomic ordering.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 under controlled cooling in an inert environment.
A lack of systematic cooling-rate dependence in both phase composition and chemical ordering would falsify the proposed cooling-rate-controlled mechanism.
